definitions.explanation: A flammable hydrocarbon liquid commonly used as fuel for heating, lamps, and some stoves in Japan.

examples.japanese: ⟦{冬|ふゆ}→冬：00623_fuyu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{灯油|とうゆ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{需要|じゅよう}→需要：02616_juyou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{増|ふ}える→増える：01183_fueru⟧。
examples.english: Demand for kerosene increases in winter.

examples.japanese: {灯油|とうゆ}⟦ストーブ→ストーブ：02906_sutoobu⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{部屋|へや}→部屋：00507_heya⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{暖|あたた}める→暖める：01858_atatameru⟧。
examples.english: I heat the room with a kerosene heater.

examples.japanese: {灯油|とうゆ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}いに→買う：00489_kau⟧⟦{行|い}かなければ→行く：00119_iku⟧。
examples.english: I need to go buy kerosene.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE: {灯油|とうゆ} heaters ({灯油|とうゆ}⟦ストーブ→ストーブ：02906_sutoobu⟧/⟦{石油|せきゆ}→石油：01448_sekiyu⟧⟦ストーブ→ストーブ：02906_sutoobu⟧) are very common in Japan, especially in areas without central heating. In winter, trucks drive around neighborhoods selling kerosene with distinctive jingles.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {灯油|とうゆ}⟦ストーブ→ストーブ：02906_sutoobu⟧ (kerosene heater)
- {灯油|とうゆ}⟦タンク→タンク：23095_tanku⟧ (kerosene tank/container)
- {灯油|とうゆ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{入|い}れる→入れる：01098_ireru⟧ (to fill with kerosene)
- {灯油|とうゆ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{値段|ねだん}→値段：00871_nedan⟧ (kerosene price)

ALTERNATE TERM: ⟦{石油|せきゆ}→石油：01448_sekiyu⟧ can also refer to kerosene in everyday contexts, though technically it means 'petroleum' more broadly.

SAFETY: Proper ventilation is required when using kerosene heaters indoors to prevent carbon monoxide poisoning.
